title: Swiggy Loss Narrows Year on Year, Widens Sequentially in Q2
excerpt: Swiggy's revenue rose 36.1% year on year to Rs 7,571 crore in Q2 FY27. Its Rs 922 crore loss was smaller than a year ago but larger than Q1, as Instamart losses offset record food delivery profit.
body:
• Swiggy's Q2 FY27 net loss narrowed year on year to Rs 922 crore from Rs 1,092 crore, but widened sequentially from Rs 791 crore in Q1 FY27.
  • Revenue from operations rose 36.1% year on year to Rs 7,571 crore, and 11.1% sequentially, as food delivery, Instamart and supply chain all grew.
  • Food delivery was the profit engine, with a segment result of Rs 349 crore, while Instamart's segment loss widened to Rs 764 crore.
  • Investors can check the full filing and segment breakdown in Swiggy's regulatory disclosure, summarised in the earnings reports linked in this article.

Swiggy reported a consolidated net loss of Rs 922 crore for the quarter ended 30 September 2026, narrowing from Rs 1,092 crore a year earlier but widening from Rs 791 crore in the June quarter. Revenue from operations rose 36.1% year on year to Rs 7,571 crore from Rs 5,561 crore in the same quarter last year, according to reports of its regulatory filing by Indian Television and Upstox.

Both framings circulating on Thursday are therefore correct, on different bases. Moneycontrol's headline emphasis on a narrower loss and 36% revenue growth is the year-on-year comparison. The sequential comparison, reported by Zee Business in the candidate signals and confirmed in the filings coverage, shows revenue up about 11% from Rs 6,812 crore in Q1 and the loss wider than Q1. Total income rose to Rs 7,783 crore from Rs 5,620 crore a year earlier, while total expenses rose to Rs 8,703 crore from Rs 6,711 crore, keeping the group in loss despite the top-line growth. The board approved the results on 22 October 2026.

"Our Food delivery business delivered its highest-ever profits and margins while we continue to unlock new category growth through Toing, our standalone offering for affordable meals."

— Sriharsha Majety, MD and Group CEO, Swiggy

Segment Performance: Food Delivery Carries, Instamart Weighs

Food delivery generated revenue of Rs 2,338 crore, up from Rs 1,921 crore a year earlier, and its segment result rose to Rs 349 crore from Rs 257 crore, according to Indian Television. Upstox reported food delivery gross order value grew 17.7% year on year to Rs 10,054 crore, with adjusted EBITDA up Rs 101 crore to Rs 341 crore. Swiggy kept guidance for food delivery excluding Toing unchanged at 18-20%, according to Upstox, and said Toing is now in more than 50 cities.

Quick commerce moved the other way on profit. Instamart revenue rose to about Rs 1,305 crore from Rs 980 crore a year earlier, but its segment loss widened to Rs 764 crore from Rs 735 crore, Indian Television reported. Upstox put Instamart gross order value up 31.4% year on year to Rs 9,230 crore, with 69 dark stores added in the quarter to reach 1,240 stores across 133 cities and total dark store area above 5.2 million square feet.

Supply chain and distribution, through Scootsy, remained the largest revenue contributor at Rs 3,690 crore, up from Rs 2,560 crore, with a segment loss narrowing to Rs 7 crore from Rs 18 crore.

Costs and User Growth

The cost lines explain the sequential widening. Advertising and sales promotion rose to Rs 1,298 crore from Rs 1,039 crore a year earlier, delivery and related charges rose to Rs 1,895 crore from Rs 1,426 crore, and purchases of stock-in-trade rose to Rs 3,607 crore from Rs 2,330 crore, according to Indian Television. Employee benefit expense eased slightly to Rs 676 crore from Rs 690 crore. Adjusted EBITDA loss was Rs 760 crore, according to Upstox.

Scale indicators still rose. Average monthly transacting users grew 21% year on year to 27.8 million, and business-to-consumer gross order value grew 24.6% to Rs 20,793 crore, Upstox reported. For the first half of FY27, revenue from operations reached Rs 14,383 crore, up from Rs 10,522 crore, and the half-year consolidated loss narrowed to Rs 1,713 crore from Rs 2,289 crore, according to Indian Television.

What Comes Next

The question for investors is whether food delivery profit and supply chain improvement can offset Instamart and new-business losses without slowing growth. Majety, quoted by Upstox, said in quick commerce the company delivered accelerated growth as guided and obtained approvals to qualify as an Indian owned and controlled company, with the transition underway, and argued differentiation on assortment would decide winners as speed and selection become standard.

Upstox noted shares fell as much as 7.13% intraday on Thursday to Rs 207.70 on the National Stock Exchange before results were declared after market close, with market capitalisation cited at Rs 58,353.03 crore as of 22 October. The next tests are sequential: whether Instamart losses stop widening as its store network matures, whether advertising spend at Rs 1,298 crore moderates, and whether food delivery margins hold at the record level Majety described.
